title: Revealing Imperfections and Beam-Induced Damage in Protein Crystals with 4D-STEM Under Cryogenic Conditions
content: No crystal is truly perfect. Rather than being arranged in flawless stacks, unit cells can be missing, twisted, or misaligned [1]. While such imperfections are commonly characterized in inorganic crystals with high-resolution electron microscopy, protein crystals are highly sensitive to beam-induced radiolysis, rendering traditional methods impractical. Since these defects can hinder structure determination, X-ray crystallographers have instead relied on measuring the broadening of diffraction peaks as a rough gauge of the underlying crystal imperfections [2].
